customers.name: Pak Gito
customers.want: A steady income and a safe neighborhood
customers.fear: Losing his waiting spot at the end of the alley

0: One coffee, Mas. Uh, Mbak. Whoever's minding the cart these days.
Around this time I'm usually already sitting on this bench. A habit from Mbah Kardi's days.
The streets are quiet today. Passengers all order through the app now.
1: Your coffee's starting to taste like Mbah Kardi's. Not the same yet, but close.
My kid asks why I always come home late. I tell him I stop by the angkringan first.
When it rains, I take shelter here while I wait for orders. Don't chase me off, okay?
2: I told the other drivers this angkringan has come back to life.
Bu Sri used to give me free tempeh when orders were slow. Such a kind woman.
If anything happens to this cart, tell me. The other drivers and I are ready to help.
3: Without your cart, this alley feels like a street without lights.
I think of this angkringan as my second home. Thank you for sticking it out.
Whatever you decide later, I'm still your first customer.

customers.name: Bu Surti
customers.want: A lively neighborhood where everyone hears the news
customers.fear: Losing her influence in the neighborhood

0: Don't make the hot tea too sweet. Sugar's expensive, I feel sorry for you.
So how are you related to Mbah Kardi? You're not family, are you? Oh well, as long as you work hard.
I'm only stopping by for a moment. I've got a bit of news, but later.
1: Your fried tofu is getting crispy. I've already told the ladies at the savings club.
Don't listen to Bu Darmi, she always exaggerates. Unlike me.
My kid lives in Jakarta and rarely comes home. That's why I like to chat here.
2: You're like one of the neighborhood's own kids now. I'm proud of you, you know.
Sri used to ask me to taste her seasoning. My tongue is a judge's tongue.
If anyone tries anything with this cart, I'll be the first to step in.
3: Sri would be happy to see her cart looked after like this.
I'm a chatterbox, but I know who's sincere. You're sincere.
From now on, whatever news I bring, you'll hear it first.

customers.name: Mas Bayu
customers.role: Mbah Kardi's nephew, back from the city
customers.want: A business of his own that people respect
customers.fear: Failing and being seen as a show-off

0: This coffee isn't bold enough. In the city, customers would complain about coffee like this.
I'm just stopping by. Don't think I'm my uncle's spy, okay?
Still the same old cart. Nothing's been replaced yet?
1: Okay, your coffee's not bad. Not bad, I said, not good yet.
My café is quiet in the afternoons. People here would rather sit at a cart.
If you run out of sugar or coffee, just grab some from my café. Pay me later.
2: I used to be embarrassed to sell in an alley. Now, watching you, I'm rethinking that.
My uncle used to say selling isn't about profit, it's about who goes home full.
Are we rivals or friends? Eh, let's say both.
3: Thank you for looking after my uncle's cart. That should have been my job.
Someday let's create a coffee menu together. My recipe, your cart.
I'm not afraid of failing anymore. Watching you, failure is just a day that isn't over yet.

customers.name: Pak Hendra
customers.want: To build a big business complex
customers.fear: Being seen as the man who ruined the neighborhood

0: I'm just passing by. It's quite busy here, isn't it?
1: I don't hate this place. I just look at the numbers.
2: If this neighborhood had shophouses, its young people wouldn't have to leave to find work.
3: You make me doubt myself. That rarely happens.
